Christ calls Himself “gentle and humble in heart,” using the adjective from the same root (Matthew 11:29). The gentleness you cannot manufacture, the Spirit grows.

practices.title: RECKON ON THE INDWELLING
practices.body: This week, before you face a temptation, a hard task, or a weary moment, pause and reckon on the truth: “The Spirit of God dwells in me. I am not facing this on my own strength.” Deliberately lean on the indwelling Spirit rather than gritting your teeth. Practice dependence: ask the Spirit for the power you lack, and expect Him to supply it from within.

practices.title: LISTEN FOR ABBA
practices.body: When doubt tells you that you do not really belong to God, do not only argue with it doctrinally. Get quiet and listen for the deeper witness — the Spirit prompting the cry ‘Abba, Father’ in your heart. Say it: “Abba, Father.” Let the Spirit’s own testimony of your sonship be louder than your doubts. Your assurance is His work, not just your reasoning.

practices.title: TEND THE FRUIT, DON’T FORCE IT
practices.body: Pick one area where you have been trying to manufacture spiritual fruit by willpower — more patience, more love, more self-control. Instead of straining harder, turn to the Spirit: “Grow this in me; I cannot produce it, but You can.” Then keep in step with Him — in the Word, in prayer, in obedience — and trust Him to bear the fruit. Tend the soil; let the growth be His.

practices.title: KEEP THE SABBATH OF THE HEART
practices.body: The Spirit bears fruit in a branch that stays connected, not one that works harder. Set aside one hour this week with your phone off and your Bible open. Read Romans 8:9–16 and pray it back to God. Do nothing else in that hour. A man who is always producing forgets that fruit is grown.

practices.title: ASK A BROTHER WHERE HE SEES FRUIT
practices.body: You are often the last to see what the Spirit is growing in you. Ask one man who knows you well: “Where have you seen God change me?” Listen without arguing. Then thank God for it, because whatever good he names was the Spirit’s work, not your achievement.

title: Sealed with the Spirit
subtitle: indwelt, filled, and marked as His own
keyVerse: In him you also, having heard the word of the truth, the Good News of your salvation—in whom, having also believed, you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is a pledge of our inheritance, to the redemption of God’s own possession, to the praise of his glory.

passage.text: In him you also, having heard the word of the truth, the Good News of your salvation—in whom, having also believed, you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,
who is a pledge of our inheritance, to the redemption of God’s own possession, to the praise of his glory.
But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if it is so that the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if any man doesn’t have the Spirit of Christ, he is not his.
If Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is alive because of righteousness.
But if the Spirit of him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised up Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you.
So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh.
For if you live after the flesh, you must die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God.
For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”

stationsIntro: These five passages open up the gift of the Spirit — sealing, indwelling, empowering, and assuring every believer. Read each slowly. Let the truth that God lives in you land before you answer. Then sit with the word study beneath it. The thread leads back to the dust — and to the Spirit who revives a clinging soul from within.
lifeIntro: This week is about moving from white-knuckled willpower to Spirit-empowered dependence, and from anxious doubt to Spirit-given assurance. The goal is to draw on the God who lives within you. Five practices for the next seven days.
prayer: Father, You sealed me with Your Spirit, and gave Him as the pledge of my inheritance. Thank You that I am not left alone to live this life. Spirit of God, dwell in me and give me life. When I doubt that I belong, cry “Abba, Father” in my heart. Grow in me what I cannot produce — love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control. Bring me home, as You have promised. Amen.

and gave Him as the pledge of my inheritance.
Thank You that I am not left alone to live this life.
Spirit of God, dwell in me and give me life.

bottomLine: God does not save you and leave you to muster the Christian life alone. He seals you with His Spirit, lives in you, and gives Him as the pledge of your inheritance. The Spirit who raised Jesus is the Spirit who grows fruit in you and will raise your body at the last.
benediction: Brother, the gospel does not merely change your record and then leave you standing alone to somehow live the Christian life on your own fumes. It changes everything, right down to who lives inside you. Your own definition of the gospel names it: filled with the Holy Spirit. The same God who justified you does not save you from a distance and walk away. He comes to live in you. The Holy Spirit — God Himself — has taken up residence in your very life, to seal you, to fill you, and to revive the dust-clinging soul from the inside.

This is the truth so many forgiven men fail to live. They believe their sins are covered, and then they set their jaw and try to grind out the Christian life by sheer willpower, white- knuckling their obedience as though it were all up to them. But you are not left to yourself. God has put His own Spirit within you — to seal you as His own possession, marking you as belonging to Him with a seal that cannot be broken; to guarantee your inheritance, as a down payment of glory already deposited in your heart; and to be the very power for the life He calls you to. You do not have it in you to live this life — but He does, and He lives in you.

And the Spirit does not only empower; He assures. When the dust whispers that you do not really belong to God, listen for the deeper voice — the Spirit Himself, crying Abba, Father in your heart, bearing witness with your spirit that you are a child of God. Your assurance is not something you must manufacture by looking at your performance; it is the Spirit’s own testimony, given from within, deeper than your doubts. And the fruit God calls for — love, joy, peace, patience — is not a crop you squeeze out by effort but fruit the Spirit grows in a soul that abides in Him.

So when your own weakness says you cannot live this life, that you do not have the strength — lift up your eyes and answer: you are right, I do not, but the Spirit of God lives in me, and He does. When your doubts say you do not really belong — lift your eyes and listen for the Spirit crying Abba within you. When you feel dead and dry and clinging to the ground — remember that the very Spirit who raised Jesus from the tomb has made your life His home, and He is at work reviving you from the inside. Lift up your eyes, brother, from your own empty strength to the God who has come to dwell in you — the pledge, living in your chest, that He will surely bring you home.
closingVerse: God does not save you and leave you alone. He seals you with His Spirit, fills you with His presence, and cries ‘Abba, Father’ in your heart. When you cannot live this life, lift your eyes — the God who dwells in you can, and will.
carry: Where do you need to stop straining and start depending?

parts.label: PART ONE
parts.heading: SOUL DUST TO REVIVAL
pulls: Your security does not rest on your grip on God, but on God’s grip on you. You are held in two omnipotent hands — and the question is not whether your weak grip will hold, but whether the Almighty’s will. It will.
paras: You come to the last week of the study, and the gospel saves its deepest assurance for the end: that a man saved by grace is secured by grace, kept to the very end, unable to be lost. Your definition of the gospel closes with these words: secured for all eternity in Him. This is where the whole story has been driving. The One who began the good work will finish it. The hand that lifted you from the dust will not let you fall back into it. You are not merely saved; you are kept.

This is the final answer to the deepest fear of the man in the dust — the fear that he might, in the end, fall away, that his grip on God might fail, that he could yet be lost. The gospel answers: your security does not rest on your grip on God, but on God’s grip on you. Jesus said of His sheep, no one will snatch them out of my hand, and no one is able to snatch them out of the Father’s hand. You are held by two omnipotent hands. The question is not whether your weak grip will hold, but whether the Almighty’s will — and it will.

And so you return, at the last, to where the whole study began: to Eden, and the promise of Genesis 3:15. The serpent’s head has been crushed. The Deliverer promised into the dust of the fall has come, lived, died, risen, and now keeps His people to the end. The story that opened with ruin closes with a security nothing in all creation can break. This capstone week gathers up everything — the ruin, the Rescuer, the rescue, the reception — into one unshakable truth: in Christ, you are secured forever. Lift up your eyes one last time, brother, and rest in the God who will bring you all the way home.

parts.label: PART TWO
parts.heading: WHAT THIS WEEK IS AFTER
paras: You are going after the doctrine of eternal security — the final clause of the gospel definition: secured for all eternity in Him. This is the truth that the God who saves also keeps; that the good work He began He will surely complete; that nothing in all creation can separate a believer from His love. This is not presumption or license, but the deepest ground of assurance and the strongest motive for grateful obedience. A man who knows he is secured forever does not sin more freely; he loves more freely, serves more freely, and rests more deeply, because his fear of being finally lost is gone.

The goal this week, as the capstone of the whole study, is to gather up everything the gospel has given — the diagnosis of ruin, the Rescuer who came down, the cross and empty tomb, the great exchange, the peace and the Spirit — and to seal it with the assurance that it can never be undone. And to bring the study full circle, back to Genesis 3:15: the serpent promised to be crushed has been crushed, and the people the Deliverer came to save are kept to the end. A man should close this book not anxious about whether he will make it, but resting in the God who guarantees he will.

Why Start Here Because the man in the dust’s deepest, most haunting fear is that in the end he might fall away and be lost — that his grip will fail, that he will not make it home. This capstone week exists to lay that fear to rest forever, by moving a man’s confidence off his own grip and onto God’s. It gathers the whole gospel into a single unshakable assurance: the One who began the work will finish it, and nothing in all creation can separate a believer from the love of God in Christ. A man who ends this study secured forever can finally rest, and love, and serve, not from fear of loss but from the freedom of one who is safe in the everlasting hands of God.

parts.label: PART THREE
parts.heading: Held by an Unbreakable Chain
paras: In Romans 8, Paul forges a chain of divine acts so strong that no link can break. Those God foreknew, He predestined; those He predestined, He called; those He called, He justified; those He justified, He glorified. Follow it carefully: everyone who enters the chain at the beginning arrives at the end. Not most of them, not the ones who try hard enough — all of them. And notice the last link is written in the past tense: He glorified. Your final glory is so certain in the mind of God that Paul speaks of it as already done. The chain that begins in God’s eternal purpose ends in your glorification, and not one link will fail.

This is the backbone of eternal security: your salvation is God’s work from beginning to end, and God finishes what He starts. Paul says it directly elsewhere — “he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.” The same grace that saved you keeps you; the same God who justified you will glorify you. Your perseverance to the end is not finally your achievement but God’s guarantee. You will hold on, yes — but the reason you will hold on is that He is holding you, and He does not lose what the Father has given Him.

Then Paul turns to the courtroom one last time and empties it of accusers. Who shall bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies. Who is to condemn? Christ Jesus is the one who died — more than that, who was raised — who is at the right hand of God, interceding for you. See the security: the Judge Himself has justified you, so no charge can stand; and your risen Savior is at God’s right hand praying for you right now, so no condemnation can fall. The case against you cannot be reopened, because the Judge has closed it and your Advocate is pleading your cause in heaven. You are not hoping to escape condemnation; it has been made impossible.

parts.label: PART FOUR
parts.heading: Nothing Can Separate — the Serpent Crushed
paras: Paul climbs to the summit of the whole letter, and it is one of the most triumphant passages in all of Scripture. He lists everything a fearful heart could imagine might separate a believer from God — tribulation, distress, persecution, famine, danger, death, life, angels, rulers, things present, things to come, powers, height, depth — and sweeps them all away: “nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” He leaves nothing out. There is no circumstance, no power, no failure, no force in the universe that can sever a believer from the love of God. The list is exhaustive on purpose, so that no anxious soul can find one exception.

And notice where this love is anchored: “God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” You cannot be separated from it because it does not rest on your lovability or your consistency; it rests in Christ, and you are in Him. As long as Christ cannot be torn from the Father’s love — which is to say, forever — neither can you, because you are hidden in Him. Jesus said it in His own words: My sheep hear my voice, and I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand. Two hands hold you — the Son’s and the Father’s — and no power in creation can pry them open.

And so the study comes full circle. You began in the dust of Eden, where God promised that the offspring of the woman would crush the serpent’s head. Across these twelve weeks you have watched that promise unfold: the ruin the serpent caused, the Deliverer who came down, the cross where the serpent struck the heel and had his own head crushed, the empty tomb, the righteousness credited, the peace secured, the Spirit given. And now, at the last, you see the final fruit of the crushed serpent: a people the enemy can never reclaim, held forever in the hands of God. The serpent is defeated. His accusations are silenced. His grip is broken. And you, once dead in the dust and by nature a child of wrath, are now secured for all eternity in Christ, from whose love nothing in all creation can ever separate you. Lift up your eyes, brother, one final time — the promise made in the dust has been kept, the serpent’s head is crushed, and you are held, and you will be brought home.

stations.verse: Whom he predestined, those he also called. Whom he called, those he also justified. Whom he justified, those he also glorified.
note: The unbreakable chain. Every link holds, and everyone who enters at the first link arrives at the last: predestined, called, justified, glorified. There is no leakage, no falling out along the way — the same “whom … those” carries all the way through. And the final link, glorified, is in the past tense, though your glory is still future, because in the certainty of God’s purpose it is as good as done. Your salvation is a chain forged by God from eternity to eternity, and your final glory is so secure that God speaks of it as already accomplished.
stations.question: Is your final glory uncertain to you, or settled in the God who calls, justifies, and glorifies?
stations.gloss: to glorify, to bring to glory
stations.live: Read Romans 8:30 out loud once a day. When you reach “glorified,” thank God that He speaks of it as done.
body: Paul writes it in the aorist tense — ‘glorified,’ as a completed act — though the believer’s glory is still future, so certain is it in God’s purpose. The past-tense doxazō for a future event is the grammar of absolute certainty: your glorification is so sure in God’s eternal purpose that it can be spoken of as already done. Every link in the chain holds, and the last one is guaranteed. God speaks of your glory as already finished — because in His purpose, it is as good as done.

stations.verse: I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand. My Father who has given them to me is greater than all. No one is able to snatch them out of my Father’s hand.
note: Jesus grounds your security in two hands, not your own. He gives His sheep eternal life, and declares they will never perish and no one can snatch them from His hand — and then adds that they are also held in the Father’s hand, and no one is able to snatch them from there. Two omnipotent hands hold you. Your security does not depend on the strength of your grip on God, which is weak and wavering, but on the strength of His grip on you, which is almighty. The question is never whether you can hold on tightly enough, but whether God can — and He can.
stations.question: Are you resting your security on your grip on God or on His grip on you?
stations.gloss: to snatch, to seize by force, to carry off
stations.live: The next time you are afraid of falling away, open your hand and pray: “You hold me. I do not hold myself.”
body: Jesus says no one can harpazō — forcibly snatch — His sheep from His hand or the Father’s. No power can wrench a believer from the grip of God. Harpazō implies violent seizure, and Jesus denies that any such power exists that can tear His sheep away. The believer is held so securely that no force in creation — not the enemy, not circumstance, not the sheep’s own weakness — can snatch him from the double grip of Son and Father. No power can snatch you from His hand — not the enemy, not your circumstances, not even your own weakness.

stations.verse: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
note: Paul empties the universe of every possible threat and declares none of them can separate a believer from God’s love. He lists the great terrors — death, life, angels, rulers, powers, things present and to come, height, depth — and then, so nothing is missed, adds “nor any other created thing.” The love this refers to is anchored in “Christ Jesus our Lord”: you cannot be separated from it because you are in Him, and Christ can never be separated from the Father’s love. The exhaustive list is deliberate mercy — so that no fearful heart can find the one exception that undoes it. There is none.
stations.question: What “what if” most threatens your assurance, and can you place it in Paul’s list?
stations.gloss: height, a high place
stations.live: Name the height and the depth in your life right now — your best success and your worst failure. Tell God that neither one can separate you from His love.
body: Hupsōma is height — the high place. Paul names “height” and “depth” together near the end of his list. Whatever the heights mean — powers above, or your own best days — and whatever the depths mean — the grave, or your worst failures — neither “will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” No height of success and no depth of failure can take you out of His love.

stations.verse: being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.
note: Paul’s confidence rests not on the Philippians’ ability to persevere but on God’s commitment to finish what He started. He who began the good work — God, who began your salvation — will complete it. Your salvation is a project God undertook, and God does not abandon His projects half-built. The same grace that began the work guarantees its completion at the day of Christ. Your perseverance is real, but underneath it is God’s preservation: you will finish because He will finish you. The good work is His, and so is its completion.
stations.question: Where do you fear the work of grace in you might stall?
stations.gloss: to begin, to make a beginning
stations.live: Look back over one year of your life and name one thing God has begun in you. Thank Him that He will finish it.
body: Enarchomai means to begin. It appears only twice in the New Testament, both times in Paul. In Galatians 3:3 he asks men who began by the Spirit whether they will now be completed by the flesh. In Philippians 1:6 he says the One who began the good work in you will complete it. The same God begins and completes. Your salvation did not start with you, and it will not be left for you to finish. The God who began the work in you did not begin it to abandon it.

stations.verse: Now to him who is able to keep them from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory in great joy…
note: The study ends where the gospel ends: with God able to keep you and bring you home. Jude does not say you are able to keep yourself; he says God “is able to keep them from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory in great joy.” Picture the end of the road: not a weary sinner barely limping across the line, but a believer presented faultless, in the presence of God’s glory, and the whole scene marked by great joy. This is where the God who lifted you from the dust is taking you. He is able to keep you, and He will present you home.
stations.question: What would it mean to live the rest of your days sure of how your story ends?
stations.gloss: to guard, to keep, to watch over and protect
stations.live: Tell someone this week how you expect your story to end, and give God the credit for keeping you.
body: God is able to phulassō — guard and keep — the believer from stumbling and bring him safely to glory. Phulassō is the word for a watchful guard protecting what is entrusted to him. Your final safe arrival is guaranteed not by your vigilance but by God’s guarding. He keeps what is His, and will present the kept ones faultless, in great joy, at the end. You will arrive home not because your grip held, but because your God guarded you all the way.

practices.title: MOVE YOUR GRIP TO HIS
practices.body: This week, when the fear of falling away or not making it home rises up, deliberately move your confidence off your own grip and onto God’s. Say: “I am held in two omnipotent hands. The question is not whether my grip will hold, but whether His will — and it will.” Practice resting your security on God’s hold on you, not your hold on Him.

practices.title: ANSWER EVERY ‘WHAT IF’
practices.body: Name the specific fear that most threatens your assurance — your ‘what if.’ Then place it into Romans 8:38–39 and answer it: “Not even this can separate me from the love of God in Christ. Paul already searched all creation, and there is nothing.” Preach the exhaustive list over your one exception until it loses its power.

practices.title: SERVE FROM SECURITY, NOT FOR IT
practices.body: Now that the study is ending, take one way you will live differently — one act of obedience, love, or service — and do it from your security, not for it. Say: “I am secured forever in Christ. I do this not to keep my salvation, but out of the freedom of one who cannot lose it.” Let the assurance of being kept forever become the engine of grateful, unafraid obedience.

practices.title: WRITE YOUR TESTIMONY IN FIVE LINES
practices.body: Take a sheet of paper and write five lines: where God found you, what He did in Christ, what He has done in you since, where you are right now, and how Romans 8:30 says your story ends. Keep it short and plain. Put it in your Bible. On the day you doubt, read it — not as proof of your faithfulness, but of His.

practices.title: BRING ANOTHER MAN THROUGH THIS STUDY
practices.body: The man who has been kept learns to help keep others. This week, ask one man if he would walk through these twelve weeks with you from the beginning. You are not his savior; you are his brother. Start at Week One with him, in the dust, and walk toward the same end: held in the hands of God, brought home.

title: Secured Forever
subtitle: kept to the end — the serpent crushed
keyVerse: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

passage.text: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.
For whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers.
Whom he predestined, those he also called. Whom he called, those he also justified. Whom he justified, those he also glorified.
What then shall we say about these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
He who didn’t spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how would he not also with him freely give us all things?
Who could bring a charge against God’s chosen ones? It is God who justifies.
Who is he who condemns? It is Christ who died, yes rather, who was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us.
Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Could oppression, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?
Even as it is written, “For your sake we are killed all day long. We were accounted as sheep for the slaughter.”
No, in all these things, we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.
For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.
My Father who has given them to me is greater than all. No one is able to snatch them out of my Father’s hand.
I and the Father are one.”

stationsIntro: These five passages open up the security of the believer — kept by God, held by two hands, unable to be separated from His love, brought all the way home. Read each slowly. Let the assurance land before you answer. Then sit with the word study beneath it. The thread leads back to the dust one last time — and to the God whose grip does not fail.
lifeIntro: This is the capstone week of the whole study, so the application is about resting your entire future on the God who keeps you — and letting that security free you to love and serve without fear. Five practices for the days ahead.
prayer: Father, You predestined, called, justified, and glorified me. You speak of my glory as already done. I am held in the Son’s hand and in Yours, and no one can snatch me out. Nothing in all creation can separate me from Your love in Christ. You began a good work in me, and You will complete it. Keep me from stumbling, and present me faultless before Your glory. To You be the glory, now and forever. Amen.

bottomLine: A man saved by grace is kept by grace. The God who called and justified you has already spoken of your glory as done; two hands hold you, and nothing in all creation can separate you from His love in Christ. You will arrive home not because you held on, but because He keeps you.
benediction: Brother, you have reached the last page of the study, and the gospel has saved its deepest assurance for the end: a man saved by grace is kept by grace, held to the very last, unable to be lost. Your own definition of the gospel closes with these words — secured for all eternity in Him — and this is where the whole story has been driving from the beginning. The hand that reached into the dust and lifted you will not let you fall back into it. The God who began this good work in you will complete it. You are not merely saved. You are kept.

This is the final answer to your deepest fear — the haunting ‘what if I don’t make it, what if my grip fails, what if I fall away in the end.’ Hear the gospel’s answer one last time: your security does not rest on your grip on God, but on God’s grip on you. Jesus holds you in His hand, and no one can snatch you from it; the Father holds you in His hand, and no one is able to snatch you from there. Two omnipotent hands enfold you, and no power in all creation can pry them apart. Paul searched the whole universe for the thing that could separate you from the love of God in Christ — death, life, powers, height, depth, any other created thing — and found nothing. There is nothing. The list is empty.

And so you end where you began. Twelve weeks ago you started in the dust of Eden, and heard God promise that the offspring of the woman would crush the serpent’s head. You have watched that promise unfold across the whole study — the ruin the serpent brought, the Deliverer who came down, the cross where the serpent struck the heel and had his own head crushed, the empty tomb, the righteousness credited, the peace secured, the Spirit given. And now you see the last fruit of the crushed serpent: a people he can never reclaim, held forever in the hands of God. The promise made in the dust has been kept. The serpent’s head is crushed. And you, once dead in the dust and by nature a child of wrath, are now secured for all eternity in Christ.

So lift up your eyes, brother — one final time, and then keep them lifted for the rest of your days. When the dust says you will never make it home, lift your eyes to the two hands that hold you and the God who completes what He begins. When your own weakness says you cannot hold on, lift your eyes and remember it was never your grip that saved you, and it is not your grip that keeps you. You will arrive home not because you held on, but because He guarded you all the way, and He will present you faultless before His glory in great joy. The soul that once clung to the dust has been revived according to His word — and it is held, and it will be brought home. Lift up your eyes, and rest. You are secured forever in Him.
closingVerse: You began this study dead in the dust; you end it secured forever in Christ. The serpent’s head is crushed, the promise is kept, and you are held in two omnipotent hands from which nothing in all creation can tear you. Lift up your eyes — you will be brought home.
